entities.summary: Shō Sei was the fifth son of King Shō Shin, who he succeeded as king of the Ryukyu Kingdom from 1526 to 1555. Born in 1497, Shuri, he ruled over a kingdom that had recently been re-established after the decline of the Ryukyu Kingdom's power in the 15th century. Shō Sei's reign was marked by efforts to strengthen the kingdom's economy and military, as well as its diplomatic relations with neighboring kingdoms. He also oversaw the construction of several major buildings, including the Shō Sei Palace, which still stands today. Shō Sei's legacy is significant, as he played a key role in the re-establishment of the Ryukyu Kingdom and its resurgence as a major power in the region. He was succeeded by his brother, King Shō In, who continued his policies. Shō Sei died in 1555, leaving behind a legacy that continues to be celebrated in Ryukyu Kingdom history. The Ryukyu Kingdom's independence was eventually lost to Japan in the late 19th century, but Shō Sei's rule remains an important chapter in the kingdom's history.
